notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals (the printed aggregate total adds all three).

The elements sum to the regiment recap (205 / 1,842 / 69; aggregate 2,116): officers 43 + 10 + 9 + 10 + 11 × 9 + 9 + 25 = 205, EP 97 + 21 + 110 + 117 + 11 × 115 + 112 + 120 = 1,842, civilians 6 + 4 + 14 + 13 + 11 + 7 + 14 = 69. The 2025 regiment chart prints no strength figures, so the check is against the recap by grade. The Signal Battalion is drawn with (x11); its basis of allocation reads eleven Signal Battalions. Battalion totals are taken from page 4 (recap by grade) of each battalion file; each battalion has its own plate.

Mission: to provide signal support for the command, control and administration of the Philippine Army. Basis of allocation: one Signal Regiment, PA. Mobility 50%. Capabilities include technological standards and doctrine on signal operations, signal units for HPA, Infantry Divisions and other major PA units, multi-level repair and maintenance of signal equipment, and fighting as infantry when required.

The HHC totals 43 / 97 / 6 (aggregate 146): Regiment Headquarters 40 / 68 / 5 (113) plus Headquarters Company 3 / 29 / 1 (33), each equal to its recap and to the grade rows of its UMD. The 17 office subtotals printed in the Regiment Headquarters UMD add to 113; the Office of the Chief of Staff has no subtotal of its own (its 2 positions are inside the 4 printed for the Secretary of the General Staff office), so the 1 / 1 split of those two offices is read from the billet rows. HHC mission: command, control and administration of the Regiment; basis of allocation one HHC; mobility 50%.

Dual designations (not counted): in the Regiment Headquarters, 6 officers, 2 EP and 3 civilians are printed in parentheses (Chief OESPA, the three SCDO section chiefs, GAD section chief, pre-audit section chief; assistant public accountability NCO and PAP monitoring NCO; Administrative Officer II and two Engineer II posts). No element has all its positions in parentheses, so no element carries dual figures. The Signal School has two O3 positions in parentheses (assistant heads of the Academic and Non-Academic Departments).

The Signal School totals 10 / 21 / 4 (aggregate 35): Headquarters 6 / 12 / 3 (Command Section 3 / 4, Administrative and Logistics Section 2 / 4, Operations and Training Section 1 / 4 / 3 civilians), Academic Department 1 / 3, Non-Academic Department 1 / 3, Doctrine and Research Department 2 / 3 / 1. Mission: specialized C4S education and training for PA personnel; one school for the Regiment; mobility 50%.

Compared with the 2019 entry (169 / 1,713 / 55): the 2025 regiment is 205 / 1,842 / 69. The new Cyber Battalion (25 / 120 / 14) is the largest change; the 2019 TO had no Cyber Battalion and kept cyber security as a company of the Network Enterprise Technology Battalion, which no longer appears in the 2025 NET Battalion. HHC rises from 34 / 87 / 6 to 43 / 97 / 6 (Regiment Headquarters 31 / 59 / 5 to 40 / 68 / 5; Headquarters Company 3 / 28 / 1 to 3 / 29 / 1). The Signal School rises from 9 / 21 / 4 to 10 / 21 / 4 and its 2019 Mobile Training Team box is not on the 2025 chart. The NET Battalion goes from 9 / 118 / 13 to 10 / 117 / 13. The Command Signal Battalion (9 / 110 / 14), Signal Battalion x11 (9 / 115 / 1) and Signal Installation and Maintenance Battalion (9 / 112 / 7) keep their 2019 totals. Net change: +36 officers, +129 EP, +14 civilians.

notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals.

Company totals sum to the battalion: officers 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 9, EP 19 + 44 + 30 + 17 = 110, civilians 0 + 14 + 0 + 0 = 14, total allowance 23 + 60 + 32 + 18 = 133. These equal the battalion recap (9 / 110 / 14, aggregate 133) and each company recap, and the grade rows of the four company UMDs add up to the battalion recap row by row. The charts print no strength figures, so there is no chart cross-check.

The headquarters and headquarters company is 4 / 19: battalion headquarters 4 / 13 (headquarters section 2 / 2, S1 and Adjutant 0 / 2, S2 0 / 2, S3 1 / 2, S4 1 / 2, supply section 0 / 2, finance section 0 / 1) plus headquarters company 0 / 6 (company headquarters 3, motor pool section 3). The chart draws the supply and finance sections as unlabelled symbol boxes; they are named from the UMD. The Command Communications Company is 2 / 44 with 14 civilians (company headquarters 1 / 5; HPA Communications Center Operations Platoon 1 / 11 including the Telephone Console Section with its 14 civilian console positions; Command Communications Platoon 0 / 17; Fixed and Wireless Communications Platoon 0 / 11). The Command Electronics Company is 2 / 30 (company headquarters 2 / 5; Public Address System Platoon 0 / 20 with a fixed squad of 5 and two mobile squads of 7; Photo and Video Coverage Platoon 0 / 5). The Command Information Technology Company is 1 / 17 (company headquarters 1 / 4; Network Installation and Maintenance Platoon 0 / 13 in four squads of 3 plus 1 platoon NCO; Electronic Warfare Platoon 0 counted). The UMD prints the two Mobile PAS Squads as one block of totals; the tree shows the count for one squad.

Mission: provide signal support to HPA, post units and other PA units in the NCR; the capabilities are installing, operating and maintaining communications, electronic and information technology systems for them, and fighting as infantry when necessary. Designation: Combat Support Unit. Basis of allocation: one Command Signal Battalion for the Signal Regiment, PA; one Headquarters and Headquarters Company, one Command Communications Company, one Command Electronics Company and one Command Information Technology Company per battalion. Mobility is 50% for the battalion and for every company.

Dual designations (not counted) total 9 officers and 25 EP. Headquarters and headquarters company 5 officers / 4 EP: the S1 and Adjutant, S2, responsible supply officer, disbursing officer and company commander; the liaison NCO, S3 information systems specialist NCO, and the operations and security NCO and supply NCO of the company headquarters. Command Communications Company 1 officer / 3 EP: the operations and security NCO, the command communications officer, the AOC squad assistant chief and the outside plant operations squad chief. Command Electronics Company 1 officer: the PAS officer. Command Information Technology Company 2 officers / 18 EP: the executive officer / RSO, personnel NCO and operations and security NCO of the company headquarters; the assistant system management specialist, assistant network administrator and assistant system analyst; and the whole Electronic Warfare Platoon (1 officer, 13 EP).

The Electronic Warfare Platoon of the Command Information Technology Company (EW officer and NCO, Electronic Support Measures squad, Electronic Countermeasures squad and Electronic Counter-Countermeasures squad, 14 positions) is entirely in parentheses, so it adds no strength. The Command Electronics Company mission also lists limited electronic warfare operations in support of HPA.

Compared with the 2019 entry (9 / 110 = 119, 14 civilians, 133 aggregate): the totals and every company (4 / 19, 2 / 44 / 14, 2 / 30, 1 / 17) are unchanged, as are the sections, platoons and squads and the dual-designated Electronic Warfare Platoon (14 positions). The 2025 TOE prints only a Required column, so the 2019 reduced EP figure (106) has no counterpart. The tree now groups the headquarters sections under a battalion headquarters and the company headquarters and motor pool under a headquarters company, and shows the platoon headquarters of the Electronic Warfare Platoon as its own dual-designated element.

notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals.

Company totals sum to the battalion: officers 3 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 10, EP 24 + 37 + 29 + 27 = 117, civilians 1 + 5 + 5 + 2 = 13, total allowance 28 + 44 + 36 + 32 = 140. These equal the battalion recap (10 / 117 / 13, aggregate 140) and each company recap, and the grade rows of the four company UMDs add up to the battalion recap row by row. The charts print no strength figures, so there is no chart cross-check.

The headquarters and headquarters company is 3 / 24 with 1 civilian: battalion headquarters 3 / 14 (headquarters section 1 / 3, S1 and Adjutant 1 / 2 with the civilian administrative officer, S2 0 / 2, S3 1 / 3, S4 0 / 3, finance section 0 / 1) plus headquarters company 0 / 10 (company headquarters 4, supply section 2, motor pool section 4). The Systems Management and Operations Company is 2 / 37 with 5 civilians (company headquarters 1 / 5; Network Operations Platoon 1 / 17 with 4 civilians, in LAN and WAN operations sections of 8 EP each; Information Systems Management Platoon 0 / 8 with 1 civilian; Web Management Platoon 0 / 7). The Information Systems Development Company is 2 / 29 with 5 civilians (company headquarters 1 / 5; Information Systems Development Platoon 1 / 14 with 2 civilians; Information Systems Analysis Platoon 0 / 7 with 1; Quality Assurance Platoon 0 / 3 with 2). The Network Management Operations Company is 3 / 27 with 2 civilians (company headquarters 2 / 5; Wide Area Network Platoon 0 / 7 with 1 civilian; Local Area Network Platoon 0 / 10; Network Monitoring and Security Platoon 1 / 5 with 1 civilian).

Mission: operate, maintain, enhance and secure the Army IT infrastructure in support of the mission of the Signal Regiment, PA; capabilities include providing information systems facilities and services to the Philippine Army, planning, deploying, operating and securing Army information systems, providing IT services and interconnectivity to PA units, and fighting as infantry when necessary. Designation: Combat Support Unit. Basis of allocation: one Network Enterprise Technology Battalion for the Signal Regiment, PA; one Headquarters and Headquarters Company, one Systems Management and Operations Company, one Information Systems Development Company and one Network Management Operations Company per battalion. Mobility is 50% for the battalion and for every company.

Dual designations (not counted) total 16 officers and 4 EP. Headquarters and headquarters company 8 officers / 2 EP: the executive officer, S2, training officer, S4, supply officer / battalion RSO, disbursing officer, and the company commander and executive officer / RSO; the liaison NCO and the assistant mess NCO. Systems Management and Operations Company 3 officers: the executive officer and RSO, the Information Systems Management officer and the Web Management officer. Information Systems Development Company 3 officers / 1 EP: the executive officer / RSO, Information System Analysis officer and Quality Assurance officer; the operations and security NCO. Network Management Operations Company 2 officers / 1 EP: the Wide Area Network and Local Area Network platoon leaders and one WAN technician. No element of this battalion is entirely dual-designated.

Printed-document points. The basis of allocation of the Information Systems Development Company calls it the Information Technology and Development Company, while its title, chart and mission use Information Systems Development Company; the title is used here. The UMD of that company prints the first sergeant at E6 and the personnel NCO at E7, which the recap (one E7, one E6) matches. The three Information Systems Development Platoon programmer lines (E4 × 4, E3 × 4, E3 × 4) are one platoon on the chart with no sections beneath it. In the Wide Area Network and Network Monitoring and Security platoons the civilian IT officer and network engineer are printed after the squad rows; they are counted at platoon level in the platoon headquarters positions. The UMD page of the Network Management Operations Company is headed Network Enterprise Technology Company, NETB. Both battalion-level documents are printed with the number G2-06-4, the same number as the Command Signal Battalion; the companies are G2-06-5.

Compared with the 2019 entry (9 / 118 = 127, 13 civilians, 140 aggregate): the total allowance is the same 140 and the military total the same 127, but the officers rise by 1 and the EP fall by 1 (10 / 117). The headquarters and headquarters company (3 / 24 / 1), the Systems Management and Operations Company (2 / 37 / 5) and the Information Systems Development Company (2 / 29 / 5) are unchanged down to their platoons and sections. The 2019 Cyber Security Company (2 / 28 with 2 civilians: company headquarters, Network and Systems Security Platoon, Computer Emergency Response Platoon, Research and Development Section) is not in the 2025 battalion; a Network Management Operations Company (3 / 27 with 2 civilians, wide area network, local area network and network monitoring and security platoons) takes the fourth company slot. The 2025 TOE prints only a Required column, so the 2019 reduced EP figure (110) has no counterpart. The tree groups the headquarters sections under a battalion headquarters and a headquarters company.

notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals.

Elements sum to the battalion: officers 6 + 0 + 3 + 0 = 9, EP 14 + 29 + 50 + 22 = 115, civilians 0 + 1 + 0 + 0 = 1, total allowance 20 + 30 + 53 + 22 = 125. These equal the battalion recap (9 / 115 / 1, aggregate 125) and the four company recaps (HHC 6 / 14 / 0 = 20, Command Signal 0 / 29 / 1 = 30, Brigade Support 3 / 50 / 0 = 53, Signal Installation and Maintenance 0 / 22 / 0 = 22). Each company UMD aggregate equals its recap, and the grade rows of the four company recaps added together equal the battalion recap row by row (O5 1, O4 2, O3 2, O2 4; E8 1, E7 3, E6 7, E5 17, E4 34, E3 48, E2 5; SG04 1). The organizational charts print no strength figures, so there is no chart cross-check.

Headquarters and Headquarters Company 6 / 14: command 2 / 1, S1 and Adjutant 1 / 2, intelligence 1 / 1, operations 1 / 1, logistics 1 / 2, company headquarters 0 / 3, supply 0 / 2, motor pool 0 / 2. Dual designations not counted: company commander and executive officer (2 officers); counter-intelligence NCO, EW NCO, training and civil-military operations NCO, frequency spectrum NCO, procurement NCO, finance NCO and records NCO (7 EP). The chart draws the battalion headquarters and the headquarters company (company headquarters, motor pool); the supply section is on the UMD only.

The Command Signal Company counts 29 EP and 1 civilian: company headquarters 3, Main Signal Support Platoon 18 (platoon NCO 1, message center 4, electronics squad 3, information system team 4, console squad 6 plus the one civilian, an Administrative Aide IV (CEO I), SG04) and the Tactical Command Post (TAC CP) Signal Support Section 8. The chart labels that section “TAP CP”. The company commander, executive officer, main platoon leader, TAC CP signal officer, encoder and messenger, and audio and video technician are dual designations and are not counted.

The Rear Signal Support Platoon is printed entirely in parentheses (dual designation) and adds nothing to the counted strength. Its dual positions are 1 officer, 19 EP and 1 civilian (the telephone operators, SG08): platoon leader 1, platoon NCO 1, message center team 6, electronics squad 4, information system team 4, console squad 4 EP and 1 civilian.

The Brigade Support Signal Company counts three identical platoons (one officer and 15 EP each: the officer and 3 EP in platoon headquarters, plus four teams of 3). The UMD heads the platoon “(x3)” and prints its lines as totals for all three; the chart draws one platoon with no quantity. The PABX specialist (1), cable splicer (3) and lineman (2) are totals for the three platoons, which gives each Wires and Cable Team 3 EP. Each platoon also has an IT specialist (E2), an audio and video operator and a network specialist in parentheses (9 EP in total), not counted. The company commander and executive officer are dual designations.

The Signal Installation and Maintenance Company counts 22 EP: company headquarters 3, Communications Installation and Maintenance Platoon 9 (headquarters positions 2, radio communications support squad 4, fixed communications support squad 3), Information Technology Support Platoon 7 (headquarters positions 2, software 2, hardware 1, network 2) and Electronics Support Platoon 3 (headquarters 1, CFS and EW support 2). Its five officer positions (company commander, executive officer, three platoon or team leaders) and three EP positions (software analyst 1, hardware specialist 2) are printed in parentheses and are not counted.

Mission: to provide signal support to the Headquarters of the Infantry Division and Infantry Brigades. Basis of allocation: eleven Signal Battalions for the Signal Regiment, PA; one HHC and one each of the Command Signal, Brigade Support Signal and Signal Installation and Maintenance Companies per battalion. Mobility: 50% (also 50% for the HHC and every company).

Compared with the 2019 entry (9 / 115 / 1, total allowance 125) the numbers do not change: HHC 6 / 14, Command Signal Company 0 / 29 / 1, Brigade Support Signal Company 3 / 50, Signal Installation and Maintenance Company 0 / 22, and the same dual-designation pattern (Rear Signal Support Platoon, company commanders and executive officers, five officer positions in the maintenance company). Section names follow the 2025 UMD (“Intelligence section” and “Logistics section” where the 2019 entry says “S4 section”).

notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals.

Elements sum to the battalion: officers 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 9, EP 24 + 29 + 29 + 30 = 112, civilians 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 7, total allowance 31 + 32 + 32 + 33 = 128. These equal the battalion recap (9 / 112 / 7, aggregate 128) and the four company recaps (HHC 6 / 24 / 1 = 31, Communications 1 / 29 / 2 = 32, Electronics 1 / 29 / 2 = 32, Information Technology 1 / 30 / 2 = 33). Each company UMD aggregate equals its recap, and the grade rows of the four company recaps added together equal the battalion recap row by row (O5 1, O4 1, O3 6, O2 1; E8 1, E7 4, E6 10, E5 14, E4 18, E3 46, E2 19; SG18 5, SG8 1, SG5 1). The organizational charts print no strength figures, so there is no chart cross-check.

Headquarters and Headquarters Company 6 / 24 / 1: command 2 / 2, S1 and Adjutant 1 / 3, S2 0 / 3, S3 1 / 4, S4 1 / 4, company headquarters 1 / 4, maintenance section 0 / 4 plus one civilian (Administrative Aide V (Carpenter II), SG05). The battalion S2 officer, the RSO, the company executive officer, the SDO and the disbursing officer (5 officers), four EP positions (publication and reproduction NCO, training and GSMO NCO, supply NCO, mess NCO) and one civilian (Administrative Aide I (Utility Worker I), SG01) are printed in parentheses and are not counted. The chart draws only the battalion headquarters (command, S1, S2, S3, S4) and the company headquarters; the maintenance section is on the UMD only.

Communications Installation and Maintenance Company 1 / 29 / 2: company headquarters 1 officer, 4 EP and two Administrative Officer V (Information Officer III) at SG18; Radio Communications IMR platoon 12 (platoon sergeant 1, tactical radio squad 6, commercial radio squad 5); Fixed Communications IMR platoon 13 (platoon sergeant 1, CAFAC squad 5, wireless facilities squad 7). The executive officer and the two platoon leaders (3 officers) and the billets for antenna specialists, copper cable, telephone, microwave and IP radio technicians are printed in parentheses and are not counted.

Electronics Installation and Maintenance Company 1 / 29 / 2: company headquarters 1 officer, 4 EP and two civilians (Senior Defense Research Officer SG18, Electronics and Communication Equipment Technician II SG08); Electronics IMR platoon 13 (platoon sergeant 1 plus two squads of 6; the UMD prints the squad lines as “(2x)” totals); Combat Fighting System Support platoon 12 (platoon sergeant 1, NFS equipment IMR squad 7, research and development squad 4). The Electronic Warfare Support Platoon is printed entirely in parentheses and adds nothing: 1 officer, 15 EP and 5 civilians in dual designations (repair and maintenance squad 4 EP and 2 civilians, installation squad 4 EP and 3 civilians, mobile EWS squad 6 EP, plus the platoon leader and platoon sergeant). Other parenthesised billets (executive officer, two platoon leaders, cable and satellite TV, RAC and electrician technicians, researchers) are not counted.

Information Technology Installation and Maintenance Company 1 / 30 / 2: company headquarters 1 officer, 4 EP and two Computer Programmer III at SG18; IT Equipment IMR platoon 13 (platoon sergeant 1, software squad 5, hardware squad 7); Network IMR platoon 13 (platoon sergeant 1, wired network squad 6, wireless network squad 6). The UMD prints the third squad heading as “Electronic Counter Measure Squad (x2)” but lists an ECCM chief, technician and operators, and the chart names it ECCM. In the wired network squad two lines are printed with merged labels (“Network Technician to Ethernet Switch Technician”, “Network Installer to Network Researcher”); the squads of 6 and 6 and the platoon sub-total of 13 reconcile with the recap.

Mission: to provide signal installation and maintenance support to the Philippine Army. Basis of allocation: one Signal Installation and Maintenance Battalion for the Signal Regiment, PA; one HHC and one each of the Communications, Electronics and Information Technology Installation and Maintenance Companies per battalion. Mobility: 50% (also 50% for the HHC and every company). The TOE numbers printed are G2-06-4 for the battalion and G2-06-5 for the HHC and the companies, the same numbers as the Signal Battalion documents.

Compared with the 2019 entry (9 / 112 / 7, total allowance 128) the numbers do not change at any level: HHC 6 / 24 / 1, Communications 1 / 29 / 2, Electronics 1 / 29 / 2, Information Technology 1 / 30 / 2, and the same all-dual Electronic Warfare Support Platoon (1 officer, 15 EP, 5 civilians) and Electronic Warfare Platoon (1 officer, 25 EP). Differences are in wording only, as the 2025 UMD prints it: the full platoon names (“Radio Communications Installation, Maintenance and Repair (IMR) Platoon”, “Fixed Communications Installation, Maintenance and Repair (IMR) Platoon”) and the “Combat Fighting System Support Platoon” heading. The printed title of the Electronics company basic document carries a stray “BRIGADE SUPPORT” (“Signal Installation and Maintenance Battalion Brigade Support Signal Regiment”).

notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals (the printed aggregate total adds all three).

Elements sum to the battalion: officers 10 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 25, EP 23 + 31 + 33 + 33 = 120, civilians 0 + 4 + 5 + 5 = 14, aggregate 159. These equal the battalion recap (25 / 120 / 14) and the recaps of the HHC (10 / 23 / 0, aggregate 33), CARMC (5 / 31 / 4, 40), CPDC (5 / 33 / 5, 43) and IRADC (5 / 33 / 5, 43); the grade rows of each unit manning document equal its recap and every printed UMD subtotal was re-added. The 2025 charts print no strength figures.

Mission: to conduct cybersecurity operations in order to protect the PA cyber assets from cyber-attacks across the PA domains of operation. Capabilities: identify and manage cyber assets and risks, detect attacks, protect cyber assets, respond to cyber incidents, recover lost or damaged assets and conduct countermeasures for self-defense. Basis of allocation: one Cyber Battalion for the Signal Regiment, PA; one HHC and one each of the CARMC, CPDC and IRADC. Mobility 50% for the battalion and for every company.

The HHC holds Battalion Headquarters 8 / 14 (command 2 / 3, S1 and Adjutant 1 / 3, S2 1 / 2, S3 2 / 2, S4 1 / 3, finance 1 / 1) and the headquarters company 2 / 9 (company headquarters 2 / 2, supply section 0 / 3, motor pool section 0 / 4). Each of the three companies has a company headquarters and three platoons; each platoon has one platoon leader, EP and civilian specialists (SG11, SG12, SG15 and SG16 grades).

Dual designations (not counted): 1 officer and 5 EP in the HHC are printed in parentheses (Special Disbursing Officer; Records NCO, GAD NCO, Cyber Threat Intelligence NCO, ATR NCO, Mess NCO). No element has all its positions in parentheses, so none carries dual figures, and the companies print none.

New in the 2025 TOE: the 2019 Philippine Army TO has no Cyber Battalion. In 2019 cyber security was a Cyber Security Company (2 officers, 28 EP, 2 civilians) in the Network Enterprise Technology Battalion, and the 2025 NET Battalion no longer lists a cyber company. The 2019 electronic-warfare elements are dual-designated platoons (zero counted strength) in the IT and electronics companies and have no counterpart in the Cyber Battalion.

The HHC counts are calculated from billet rows (Regiment Headquarters 31 officers / 59 EP / 5 civilians, Headquarters Company 3 / 28 / 1), and agree with the printed HHC chart figures of 34 / 87 / 6.

The ASR recap workbook also contains hidden worksheets with older draft figures (for example Command Signal Bn 9 / 151 / 39, Signal Bn 9 / 146 / 6, Signal School 4 / 21 / 8). They disagree with the visible recap and the organizational charts and are not used.

tag: PA TOE s-2025 (22 May 2025) · required strength
intro: The combat units of the Infantry Division as drawn in the 2025 annex: three brigade headquarters companies, nine infantry battalions and three division reconnaissance companies. Open a unit to see its sections and squads, including the S6 signal staff and the battalion Signal Platoon.

notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals.

Unit boxes sum to the combat units: officers 3 × 15 + 9 × 30 + 3 × 5 = 330, EP 3 × 81 + 9 × 543 + 3 × 95 = 5,415, total 3 × 96 + 9 × 573 + 3 × 100 = 5,745. Both match the division recap (330 / 5,415 / 5,745), and the grade rows of the unit manning documents multiplied by 3, 9 and 3 equal every grade row of the division recap (for example O7 3, O6 6, O5 18, O4 27, O3 111, O2 51, O1 114).

The 2025 annex covers only the combat units (BDE HHQ x3, Infantry Battalion x9, Division Reconnaissance Company x3). The Division Headquarters, military intelligence, CMO, support, training and hospital units drawn in the 2019 division are not in these documents, so the figures are not comparable with the 2019 division total of 516 / 6,528.
The 2025 chart prints no strength figures in its boxes, only the quantities x3, x9 and x3; the totals come from the recap and the unit manning documents. The annex also prints no TOE number.

Against the same three unit types in the 2019 entry (3 × 15 + 9 × 32 + 3 × 5 = 348 officers, 3 × 83 + 9 × 570 + 3 × 95 = 5,664 EP): officers are 18 fewer and EP 249 fewer. The brigade headquarters company loses 2 EP each, the infantry battalion loses its Weapons Company strength (2 officers, 56 EP) and gains 29 EP in its headquarters company, and the reconnaissance company is unchanged at 5 / 95.

The 2025 publication prints three combat-unit sets for the Infantry Divisions: this nine-battalion set (folder note: 4ID, 10ID, 11ID), a set with an Infantry Battalion (Heavy) (5ID and 2ID) and a ten-battalion set. All three use the same Brigade HHC, Infantry Battalion and Division Reconnaissance Company documents; the other two sets have their own plates on this page.

title: Infantry Battalion (2025)
tag: PA TOE s-2025 (22 May 2025) · required strength
intro: Headquarters and headquarters company with its signal, medical, intelligence, scout, sniper, mortar and support platoons, and three rifle companies. The Weapons Company is drawn dashed and carries no strength. Nine per Infantry Division.

notes: Counts are the Required strength column of the TOE s-2025. Positions printed in parentheses are dual designations and are not counted. Officers (O1–O9) and enlisted personnel (EP, E1–E9) are read from the grade rows; civilian employees (SG grades) are shown separately and are not part of personnel totals.

Elements sum to the battalion: officers 15 + 0 + 3 × 5 = 30, EP 153 + 0 + 3 × 130 = 543, total 168 + 3 × 135 = 573. These equal the battalion recap (30 / 543 / 573), the HHC recap (15 / 153 / 168) and the Rifle Company recap (5 / 130 / 135), and the grade rows of the HHC and rifle company UMDs (HHC + 3 × rifle) equal the battalion recap row by row.

The battalion Signal Platoon is 11 EP: platoon headquarters 1 (signal chief / platoon sergeant), communications section 6, electronics section 2, information systems section 2. The S6 section (signal officer, signal NCO, assistant signal NCO) is a separate 3-person staff section in the battalion headquarters, 1 officer and 2 EP. The platoon leader, supply sergeant and the electronics and information systems section chiefs are dual designations and are not counted.

Headquarters 10 / 30 plus headquarters company 5 / 123 give the HHC 15 / 153. The headquarters company holds company headquarters 7, support platoon 23 (including a 2-EP liaison section), medical platoon 17, signal platoon 11, intelligence platoon 23, scout platoon 26 and mortar platoon 21. The Sniper Section is entirely dual-designated (7 positions in parentheses) and adds 0. The UMD prints the collection teams (x3), scout teams (x3), rifle platoons (x3) and rifle squads (x9) as totals for all repeated elements; the tree shows the count for one element.

The Weapons Company is drawn as a dashed box on the battalion chart but has no basis of allocation, recap or manning document in the 2025 files, and the battalion recap equals the HHC plus three rifle companies. It is shown with no strength; its mortar platoon and sniper section now sit in the HHC.

Basis of allocation: nine Infantry Battalions per Infantry Division; one HHC per battalion (mobility 80%); three Rifle Companies per battalion (relies on the battalion headquarters). The battalion mobility is 30%. Mission: close with the enemy by fire and maneuver to destroy or capture him or repel his assault by fire, close combat and counterattack.

Compared with the 2019 entry (32 / 570 = 602): the officers drop by 2 and the EP by 27. The 2019 Weapons Company (2 / 56) is gone, the mortar platoon (21 EP) moves into the HHC, the sniper section changes from 7 counted EP to dual-designated, the S2 section gains 2 EP (5 to 7) and the intelligence platoon gains 6 EP (17 to 23: three collection teams of 7 against 4 plus a separate signal intelligence team of 3). Other HHC elements and the 5 / 130 Rifle Company are unchanged. The 2019 Heavy machine-gun platoon (18 EP) has no 2025 counterpart.
The same Infantry Battalion document is printed in all three Infantry Division combat-unit folders of the 2025 publication; the counts are identical.
